## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the two displayed Schur families generate \(J_v\), each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements, and graded Nakayama identifies minimality with inclusion-minimal spanning in \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\). [source-2, lines 1380-1421; source-2, lines 1520-1540]
- [proved] **Conditional target established.** Assume the \(p=c=1\) integral interval/Pieri presentation of task 85 and its compatible box-specialization maps. Then for every admissible \(b=\min(i,j)\ge1\) and every \(a=\min(p,c)=1\),
  \[
  Q:=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{b+1},
  \]
  and both proposed \(a=1\) families are minimal generating families.

## Strategy
Put \(p=n-r-i\), \(c=r-j\), \(d=ij\).  For \(p=c=1\), task 85 gives, for \(0\le k\le b\),
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=0}^{k}\mathbb Z C_x,\qquad
C_x=P_{x,k-x},
\]
with complete \(h_1\)-row lattice
\[
L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}).
\]
The two endpoints are
\[
Y_k=C_0=s_{(i^j,k)},\qquad
X_k=C_k=s_{((i+1)^k,i^{j-k})}.
\]

For \(1\le\ell\le k\), the boxed Pieri rule gives, for
\(0\le x\le k-\ell\),
\[
h_\ell P_{x,k-\ell-x}=C_x+C_{x+1}.
\]
Indeed, a horizontal \(\ell\)-strip can either extend the bottom part by
\(\ell\), or extend one \(i\)-row to \(i+1\) and the bottom part by
\(\ell-1\); these are the only in-box outcomes. Hence
\[
(\Lambda_+M)_{d+k}=L_k.
\]
Since deleting either endpoint column from the \(h_1\)-path matrix is
unimodular,
\[
Q_{d+k}=M_{d+k}/L_k\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad
[X_k]=(-1)^k[Y_k].
\]
Thus, for \(p=c=1\),
\[
Q\cong\bigoplus_{k=0}^{b}\mathbb Z[Y_k]
      \cong\mathbb Z^{b+1},
\]
and either endpoint family maps to a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis.

For general \(\min(p,c)=1\), use the conditional box specialization
\[
\Lambda/I_{j+c,i+p}\twoheadrightarrow\Lambda/I_{j+1,i+1}.
\]
If \(p=1\), the first source family specializes to \((X_0,\ldots,X_b)\);
if \(c=1\), the second specializes to \((Y_0,\ldots,Y_b)\). In either
case its images generate the target \(J\), so this induces a surjection
\[
Q_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow Q_{1,1}.
\]
Both source families have \(b+1\) homogeneous elements, and either maps
to the displayed basis of \(Q_{1,1}\). Therefore the induced composite
\[
\mathbb Z^{b+1}\twoheadrightarrow Q_{p,c}\twoheadrightarrow
Q_{1,1}\cong\mathbb Z^{b+1}
\]
sends the standard basis to a basis and is an isomorphism. Hence both
arrows are isomorphisms. The accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion
then makes each family inclusion-minimal.

## Gaps
The conclusion is conditional on task 85’s integral interval/Pieri presentation and on compatible specialization from the \((p,c)\)-box to the \((1,1)\)-box. Those hypotheses are not independently source-grounded here. The source itself labels the general minimality statement a conjecture. [source-2, lines 1489-1502]

## Next
An unconditional result requires a proof of the invoked box presentation and specialization compatibility.
